A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Parenting, with matching research objectives, core methods, and experiments. All 16 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v3, including appendices, support comparison through text and visual inspection.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, medical-domain transfer, noise-recognition experiments, sensitivity analyses, and memorization tests.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds general-capability evaluations, temporal and multi-hop QA experiments, closed-source model comparisons, computational measurements, and a case study.

M1.justification: Equations 10–12 change the parameter-selection Z-score cutoff from 0 to 1, revising which units receive particular updates. The importance calculation and tuning losses remain unchanged. Renaming parameter groups as subspaces and explicitly naming the frozen remainder otherwise restate existing components.

E1.justification: The original SQuAD2.0-Eval, RGB, KNOT, and CMB coverage remains. Appendix A.6 adds ARC, HellaSwag, MMLU, Winogrande, GSM8K, and TruthfulQA to assess general capabilities. Appendix A.10 adds TempReason for timestamp-dependent knowledge selection and MuSiQue for multi-hop reasoning, substantially broadening task requirements.

E2.justification: The main baseline suite remains unchanged. Appendix A.11/Table 10 adds Claude-3.5 Sonnet and GPT-4 as comparators on SQuAD2.0-Eval and KNOT. PH3 and KnowPO are additions to related work, not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The existing backbones, LoRA settings, training budgets, and RAd/RRo metrics remain. New general-capability evaluations introduce five-shot testing on five benchmarks and zero-shot TruthfulQA, with normalized accuracy, accuracy, and strict exact-match metrics. Appendix A.12 also introduces a separate comparison of probing and training time, memory, and token counts.

E4.justification: v3 adds general-capability retention tests, Qwen parameter-localization analysis, computational-overhead analysis, a confusable-document case study, and qualitative KNOT-I failure analysis. Existing ablations, sensitivity analyses, and memorization tests remain. Noise recognition moves from v1 Appendix A.6 to v3 Section 5.4 with unchanged results.

E5.justification: v3 introduces no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence-interval definitions, or significance tests. The retained plots use the same uncertainty presentation. Equation 6's unchanged uncertainty calculation concerns parameter importance rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores and the original appendix results remain unchanged. New Table 9 reports Parenting accuracies of 31.40% on TempReason and 61.35% on MuSiQue, versus KAFT's 28.70% and 58.72%. Tables 5 and 10–12 add general-capability, closed-source comparison, computational-cost, and case-study outcomes.

T1.justification: The formal parameter-set definitions in Equations 10–12 replace the zero Z-score boundary with one. The importance-score derivation and loss formulations otherwise remain substantively unchanged, and neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly claims Parenting is the first approach to fine-grained parameter-space decoupling and optimization of adherence and robustness. v3 replaces this priority claim with a claim of a novel insight. The central claims of balanced improvement and out-of-distribution generalization remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning KNOT-I implicit reasoning, matrix-level granularity, SQuAD-only training, and low-quality retrieved documents. It also interprets new results as showing limited general-capability disruption and faster training, and links the Qwen localization findings to larger models' use of internal memory.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code link, evaluation-harness information, resource measurements, and clarification that relevant baselines use the same source data. Appendix A.5's implementation recipe remains unchanged. Conversely, v1 Table 4's conflicting/irrelevant evaluation sample counts are removed, reducing reproducibility detail.

R1.justification: v3 adds PH3 and KnowPO to Section 2.2, explicitly credits Feng et al. (2024b) for parameter-localization inspiration, and cites Tang et al. (2024) for activation probing. Additional benchmark and application references extend the literature coverage, while the basic related-work organization and research niche remain.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around knowledge control and the brain/subspace analogy. Method terminology and Section 4.3 are reorganized around named subspaces. Noise recognition moves into the main text, and a limitations section and several new appendix subsections expand the document structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to map brain regions to parameter subspaces, and Figure 2 is updated. The noise-recognition table moves into the main text, while the evaluation-statistics table is removed. A new Qwen heatmap and tables for general capabilities, additional tasks, closed-source comparisons, costs, and the case study substantially expand the visual material.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens assessment of applicability through direct general-capability retention and computational-cost tests, temporal and multi-hop evaluations, and concrete limitations absent from v1. However, removing evaluation sample counts weakens reproducibility, and the selection-cutoff revision is not reconciled with the unchanged main results. The added validation and transparency support a positive but limited overall quality improvement.
